title: Crane Shed Design in Pakistan: Capacity and Span | Steel Mind Engineers
description: Learn how overhead crane loads change a steel building. Crane capacity, span, runway beams and rails, with the Haier crane sheds at Raiwind as the example.
h1: Crane Shed Basics in Pakistan: Capacity, Span and Runway Beams Explained
quickAnswer: A crane shed is a steel building designed around its overhead cranes. The crane capacity, span, lifting height and working frequency set the size of the columns, the runway beams and the foundation. Steel Mind Engineers built crane sheds of 96,600 and 97,888 square feet for Haier at Raiwind.

faq.q: Can I add a crane to a shed later?
faq.a: Only if the shed was designed for it. Say so at the quote stage, even if the crane will arrive in a later year.

faq.q: What details does the engineer need?
faq.a: The crane capacity, span, lifting height, number of cranes and working frequency.

faq.q: Can a shed carry two cranes?
faq.a: Yes, if the design includes both from the start.

blocks.text: A crane shed is a steel building with overhead cranes running on rails along its length. Factories use them to move steel, machine parts, containers and finished goods. In crane shed design in Pakistan, the crane is not an add-on. The whole structure is designed around the crane loads, because a moving load of many tons places forces on the columns, the beams and the foundation that an ordinary shed never meets. For this reason a building that was not designed for a crane cannot safely carry one.

Steel Mind Engineers built a pre-engineered crane shed of 96,600 square feet for Haier at Raiwind, 30 feet high, 184 feet wide and 525 feet long. It also built a PEB crane and mezzanine shed of 97,888 square feet for Haier, 33 feet high, 184 feet wide and 532 feet long. These projects show the scale of overhead crane shed construction that one team can handle, from the first drawing to handover, under one contract.

blocks.title: The Four Numbers That Set the Design

blocks.text: Four numbers matter most. The crane capacity is the heaviest load the crane lifts. The crane span is the distance between the crane rails. The lifting height is how high the hook must rise, which sets the clear height of the building. The working frequency tells how often the crane runs, and a busy crane places more fatigue on the structure. Give these four numbers to the engineer, and ask the crane maker for the wheel loads, because the frame is designed from them.

The crane type changes the building. A jib crane serves a circle around a column or wall, and a monorail crane moves loads along one fixed track. A semi-gantry crane runs on a rail on the building column at one end and on a floor-mounted leg at the other. A top-running crane, also called an EOT crane, runs on rails above crane beams across the width and gives the widest coverage and the highest capacity. An underhung crane hangs from the roof structure and suits lighter loads. Each arrangement is shown on the Crane System page.

The crane columns carry the runway beams through brackets or a stepped section. The runway beams hold the crane rails, and they must be strong, level and straight. Crane runway beams take loads from moving wheels, from braking and from sideways forces, so they are heavier than ordinary beams. Extra bracing resists the sideways and braking forces. Steel Mind Engineers fabricates the crane columns and beams in its Lahore factory and checks the dimensions before they are painted.

Rails must be level and straight within tight limits, or the crane wears quickly and runs badly. The factory cuts and drills the beams to the drawing, and the crew checks the alignment on site during erection. Accuracy at this stage saves years of repair. If the foundation is out of level, the engineer answers the same day, because the steel and the foundation must agree.

Crane columns carry large loads, so the foundation is designed together with the steel. The anchor bolt plan tells your foundation contractor where each bolt goes. Crane stops at the ends of the rails prevent the crane from running off. Access ladders and walkways let maintenance staff reach the rails and the crane safely. Plan these items in the first design, because adding them later is hard.

Choose a crane shed when the goods or the crane must be covered from rain and sun. Choose a gantry when the work happens in an open yard. A gantry is a steel structure that holds crane rails outdoors, with no building around it. Read the Crane Gantry Structures page for outdoor cranes. Many plants use both: a gantry in the yard and a crane shed for finished goods and machinery.
